Setting the scene

text.content: A tool-enabled agent can fail in a new way: the model may keep trying a tool because the requested task is still unresolved.

rich_text.plain_text: A tool-enabled agent can fail in a new way: the model may keep trying a tool because the requested task is still unresolved.

text.content: Imagine the loan-status service is unavailable. The agent calls it, receives an error, reasons that it still needs the status, and calls it again. Without a limit, the workflow can waste tokens and time while the client receives no useful answer.

rich_text.plain_text: Imagine the loan-status service is unavailable. The agent calls it, receives an error, reasons that it still needs the status, and calls it again. Without a limit, the workflow can waste tokens and time while the client receives no useful answer.
A production design therefore needs
two layers

text.content: a deterministic iteration cap in the AI Agent;

rich_text.plain_text: a deterministic iteration cap in the AI Agent;

text.content: a clear instruction for how to respond when a tool cannot provide a usable result.

rich_text.plain_text: a clear instruction for how to respond when a tool cannot provide a usable result.
Layer 1: Max Iterations
The n8n
AI Agent
has a
Max Iterations

text.content: option. It limits how many reasoning/tool-use cycles the model may run for one request.

rich_text.plain_text: option. It limits how many reasoning/tool-use cycles the model may run for one request.
For this Contigo exercise, set:
Options → Max Iterations = 4

text.content: Four iterations leave enough room for the simple multi-tool scenarios in this sprint while preventing long retry loops. The exact production value is a design decision, but it should always be intentional rather than unlimited.

rich_text.plain_text: Four iterations leave enough room for the simple multi-tool scenarios in this sprint while preventing long retry loops. The exact production value is a design decision, but it should always be intentional rather than unlimited.
Important:

text.content: Max Iterations is a circuit breaker, not a complete error-handling strategy. It stops the loop; the system message still needs to define what the client should hear when a tool is unavailable.

rich_text.plain_text: Max Iterations is a circuit breaker, not a complete error-handling strategy. It stops the loop; the system message still needs to define what the client should hear when a tool is unavailable.

text.content: A strong version should communicate all three requirements:

rich_text.plain_text: A strong version should communicate all three requirements:
No fabrication:

text.content: Never invent a loan status or pretend the tool succeeded.

rich_text.plain_text: Never invent a loan status or pretend the tool succeeded.
No technical leakage:

text.content: Do not expose internal errors, node names, stack traces, or implementation details.

rich_text.plain_text: Do not expose internal errors, node names, stack traces, or implementation details.
Clear next step:

text.content: Tell the client what to do instead.

rich_text.plain_text: Tell the client what to do instead.
Example:

text.content: "If a required tool is unavailable or does not return a usable result, do not guess or claim that the action succeeded. Tell the client: 'I’m unable to retrieve that information right now. Please try again later or contact your Contigo relationship manager for assistance.'"

Check for Understanding

text.content: A status tool keeps returning an unavailable result and the agent repeatedly calls it. Which safeguard should stop the reasoning loop even if the model keeps trying?

Takeaway:

text.content: Reliable tool use needs both model instructions and deterministic execution limits. Max Iterations bounds the loop; structured tool results and a precise failure instruction determine what happens next.
